tldr: `tool_choice` decides **whether** and **which** tool must be called: **`auto`** (default — the model may just answer in text), **`any`** (must call *some* tool — the model picks), **`{"type":"tool","name":…}`** (must call *that* tool), and — per the docs — **`none`**. Use `any` to **guarantee** structured output, a **forced tool** to make a step run **first** (then release it), `strict: true` + **nullable fields** + **“other”/“unclear” enums** so schemas neither break nor invent. Give each agent only its **role's 4–5 tools**. And know the docs' caveat: some models and manual extended thinking **reject forced tool use** (400).
mentalModel: tool_choice is how you hand the model a menu: “order if you like” (auto), “you must order something” (any), “you must order the soup first” (tool) — and a strict schema is the order form with boxes that only take numbers. A good form has a “none / other: ____” box; without one, people tick something wrong.
whatItIs:
The exam guide covers distributing tools and configuring `tool_choice` (Guide §6 · TS 2.3, pp.10–11) and getting structured output
through tool use and JSON schemas (TS 4.3, pp.17–18). The docs define the options and their limits.

**Sub-concepts — each with its picture to remember**

| # | Sub-concept | 🧭 Mental model | ⭐ Exam reference |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `auto` | “Order if you like” — the model may just chat. | ⭐ TS 2.3 · Knowledge 4; TS 4.3 · Knowledge 2 |
| 2 | `any` | “You must order something” — guaranteed tool call, the model picks which. | ⭐ TS 2.3 · Skill 5; TS 4.3 · Skill 2 |
| 3 | Forced `tool` | “The soup first” — sequence a step, then let the model choose again. | ⭐ TS 2.3 · Skill 4; TS 4.3 · Skill 3 |
| 4 | `none` | Menu closed. | 📘 docs only |
| 5 | Forcing not supported | Some kitchens don't take fixed orders: ask nicely (auto + instruction) and use a strict form. | 📘 docs only |
| 6 | Strict schema | A form whose boxes only accept the right type — no “two” in a number box. | ⭐ TS 4.3 · Knowledge 1 |
| 7 | Syntax ≠ semantics | A perfectly filled form can still have the wrong total. | ⭐ TS 4.3 · Knowledge 3 |
| 8 | Nullable / “other” / “unclear” | A “not stated”, “other: ____” and “not sure” box, so nobody ticks something false. | ⭐ TS 4.3 · Knowledge 4, Skills 4–5 |
| 9 | Scoped tools per agent | Give each worker their own toolbox; one shared box of 18 tools means wrong tools grabbed. | ⭐ TS 2.3 · Knowledge 1–3, Skills 1–3 |

**tool_choice: auto vs any vs forced** (the comparison CLAUDE.md requires)

| # | Aspect | `auto` | `any` | forced `{"type":"tool","name":…}` | `none` (docs) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Must a tool be called? | No — text is allowed | Yes | Yes | No tools |
| 2 | Which tool? | Model decides | Model picks one of yours | The one you name | — |
| 3 | Text before the tool call? | Often | No (prefilled) | No (prefilled) | — |
| 4 | Use it for | Normal agent turns | Guaranteed structured output, type unknown | A step that must run first | Turning tools off |
| 5 | Default when | Tools are provided | — | — | No tools are provided |
| 6 | Not supported with | — | Manual extended thinking; Opus 5.5 / Fable 5.1 / Mythos 5.1 (400) | Same | — |
| 7 | Exam reference | TS 2.3 K4 · TS 4.3 K2 | TS 2.3 S5 · TS 4.3 S2 | TS 2.3 S4 · TS 4.3 S3 | 📘 docs |

**Schema design that doesn't invent**

| # | Field situation | Schema choice | Why (guide) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Might be missing from the source | `"type": ["string", "null"]` | Prevents fabricated values (TS 4.3 S4) |
| 2 | Categories you can't fully foresee | enum + `"other"` + a `*_detail` string | Extensible (TS 4.3 K4, S5) |
| 3 | Genuinely ambiguous | enum value `"unclear"` | Honest ambiguity (TS 4.3 S5) |
| 4 | Numbers written inconsistently (“$1,240.00”) | `number` type + a normalisation rule in the description/prompt | TS 4.3 S6 |
howItWorks:
1. **Decide what must be guaranteed.** Nothing → `auto`. A tool call → `any`. A specific first step → forced tool, then release it.
2. **Check the model supports forcing.** If not (docs: Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1, Mythos 5.1, or manual extended thinking), use `auto` with
   strict tools and an explicit instruction — or structured outputs.
3. **Make extraction schemas honest:** `strict: true`, `additionalProperties: false`, nullable where data may be missing, `other` +
   detail and `unclear` in enums, normalisation rules for messy formats.
4. **Validate semantics yourself** — strict guarantees types, not that totals add up (validation/retry is TS 4.4).
5. **Distribute tools:** each agent gets its role's 4–5 tools, constrained versions of risky generic tools, and a scoped cross-role
   tool for frequent needs; complex cases go back through the coordinator.

grounding.text: tool_choice has four options: auto (Claude decides; the default when tools are provided), any (must use one of the provided tools), tool (must use the named tool), none (no tools; the default when no tools are provided).

With any or tool the API prefills the assistant message, so Claude emits no natural-language text before the tool_use block — even if asked. To get an explanation AND a tool call, use auto plus an explicit instruction in the user message.

Forced tool use isn't supported everywhere: with manual extended thinking (thinking type enabled) any/tool error; on Claude Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 any/tool return a 400 — use auto with strict tool use, or structured outputs. auto and none still work.
On models that support forcing, combine tool_choice any with strict: true to guarantee a tool is called AND its input follows the schema.

strict: true constrains sampling so tool inputs always match the input_schema (types, required fields) and the tool name is valid; strict schemas need additionalProperties: false. Without strict, Claude might pass "2" instead of 2 or omit required fields.
grounding.ref: strict-tool-use § Why strict tool use matters; How it works

grounding.text: Structured outputs guarantee schema compliance, not semantic correctness; refusals and max_tokens can still produce non-compliant output.
Subagent tools can be restricted (AgentDefinition tools); a tool left out isn't in the agent's context at all. In the Agent SDK, `tools` controls availability and allowedTools controls permission.

grounding.text: Too many tools (e.g. 18 instead of 4–5) degrade selection reliability; agents with tools outside their specialisation misuse them (a synthesis agent running web searches); scope each agent's tools to its role, with limited cross-role tools for specific high-frequency needs.

from utils.toolchoice_lab import (DOCUMENT, FORCED_TOOL_CHOICE_SUPPORTED, MODEL, TASK, create, run_agent, run_tool,
                                  submit_extraction)   # SIMULATED Messages API and agents

# strict: true -> inputs always match the schema. Nullable fields -> nothing invented when the document lacks it.
# "other" + a detail field -> categories you didn't foresee; "unclear" -> honest ambiguity.
INVOICE = {"name": "extract_invoice", "strict": True,
           "description": "Extracts an invoice: vendor, total, date, tax id and spend category.",
           "input_schema": {"type": "object", "additionalProperties": False,
                            "properties": {
                                "vendor": {"type": "string"},
                                "total": {"type": "number", "description": "A number, e.g. 1240.0 - no currency symbol"},
                                "invoice_date": {"type": ["string", "null"]},
                                "tax_id": {"type": ["string", "null"], "description": "null if the document shows no tax id - never guess"},
                                "category": {"type": "string", "enum": ["hardware", "software", "services", "other", "unclear"]},
                                "category_detail": {"type": ["string", "null"], "description": "What 'other' means"}},
                            "required": ["vendor", "total", "invoice_date", "tax_id", "category", "category_detail"]}}
CONTRACT = {"name": "extract_contract", "strict": True,
            "description": "Extracts a contract: the two parties, start date, term and fee.",
            "input_schema": {"type": "object", "additionalProperties": False,
                             "properties": {"party_a": {"type": "string"}, "party_b": {"type": "string"},
                                            "effective_date": {"type": ["string", "null"]},
                                            "term_months": {"type": ["integer", "null"]},
                                            "monthly_fee": {"type": ["number", "null"]}},
                             "required": ["party_a", "party_b", "effective_date", "term_months", "monthly_fee"]}}
METADATA = {"name": "extract_metadata", "strict": True, "description": "Extracts the vendor name and document type.",
            "input_schema": {"type": "object", "additionalProperties": False,
                             "properties": {"vendor": {"type": "string"}, "document_type": {"type": "string"}},
                             "required": ["vendor", "document_type"]}}
ENRICH = {"name": "enrich_vendor", "strict": True, "description": "Adds credit terms to a vendor record. Needs the vendor_id.",
          "input_schema": {"type": "object", "additionalProperties": False,
                           "properties": {"vendor_id": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["vendor_id"]}}


def first_choice(name=None):
    """Guarantee a tool call: any (or one named tool) - on models that support forcing."""
    if not FORCED_TOOL_CHOICE_SUPPORTED:          # docs: some models reject any/tool with a 400
        return {"type": "auto"}                   # -> auto + strict tools + an explicit instruction instead
    return {"type": "tool", "name": name} if name else {"type": "any"}


instruction = "" if FORCED_TOOL_CHOICE_SUPPORTED else " Use the matching extraction tool."

if TASK == "extract":
    # the document type is unknown -> offer every extractor and require that ONE of them is called
    r = create(model=MODEL, tools=[INVOICE, CONTRACT], tool_choice=first_choice(),
               messages=[{"role": "user", "content": DOCUMENT + instruction}])
    submit_extraction(r)

elif TASK == "pipeline":
    messages = [{"role": "user", "content": DOCUMENT + " Extract the metadata, then enrich the vendor record."}]
    choice = first_choice("extract_metadata")     # step 1: force metadata extraction to run FIRST
    for turn in range(1, 6):
        r = create(model=MODEL, tools=[METADATA, ENRICH], tool_choice=choice, messages=messages)
        print(f"turn {turn}: {r.stop_reason} {[b.name for b in r.content if b.type == 'tool_use']}")
        if r.stop_reason != "tool_use":
            break
        messages.append({"role": "assistant", "content": r.content})
        messages.append({"role": "user", "content": [
            {"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": b.id, "content": run_tool(b.name, b.input)}
            for b in r.content if b.type == "tool_use"]})
        choice = {"type": "auto"}                 # later steps: follow-up turns, the model continues on its own

else:  # distribute tools across agents
    run_agent("searcher", ["web_search", "load_document"])   # its role's tools only; load_document validates document URLs
    run_agent("synthesizer", ["verify_fact"])                 # a scoped cross-role tool for quick fact checks - no web search
variants.observe: must_extract: tool_choice any → extract_invoice is called (no text before it), total comes back as 1240.0. unknown_type: any lets the model pick extract_contract for a contract. missing_fields: tax_id null, category “other” + “maintenance”, nothing invented. metadata_first: extract_metadata (forced) → enrich_vendor(V-4471) → the model finishes on auto. scoped_tools: searcher uses web_search + load_document (which rejects the login page), synthesizer uses verify_fact. model_rejects_forcing: first_choice() falls back to auto + an explicit instruction, so extraction still happens without a 400.
variants.why: Each guarantee comes from the right lever: any for “a tool must be called”, a forced tool for “this step first”, a strict schema for types, nullable/“other” fields for honesty, scoped tool lists for role discipline — and a fallback where the docs say forcing isn't supported.

               messages=[{"role": "user", "content": DOCUMENT + instruction}])
    submit_extraction(r)

elif TASK == "pipeline":
    messages = [{"role": "user", "content": DOCUMENT + " Extract the metadata, then enrich the vendor record."}]
    choice = first_choice("extract_metadata")     # step 1: force metadata extraction to run FIRST
    for turn in range(1, 6):
        r = create(model=MODEL, tools=[METADATA, ENRICH], tool_choice=choice, messages=messages)
        print(f"turn {turn}: {r.stop_reason} {[b.name for b in r.content if b.type == 'tool_use']}")
        if r.stop_reason != "tool_use":
            break
        messages.append({"role": "assistant", "content": r.content})
        messages.append({"role": "user", "content": [
            {"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": b.id, "content": run_tool(b.name, b.input)}
            for b in r.content if b.type == "tool_use"]})
        choice = {"type": "auto"}                 # later steps: follow-up turns, the model continues on its own

else:  # distribute tools across agents
    run_agent("searcher", ["web_search", "load_document"])   # its role's tools only; load_document validates document URLs
    run_agent("synthesizer", ["verify_fact"])                 # a scoped cross-role tool for quick fact checks - no web search
variants.observe: total comes back as the string “$1,240.00” in a number field — your downstream code now has a type error. Also fails missing_fields and model_rejects_forcing; the contract extractor (still strict) is fine.
variants.why: Tool use with a JSON schema is the reliable route to structured output; strict: true is what guarantees the input matches the schema's types (docs).
variants.fix: Set strict: true (with additionalProperties: false) on extraction tools.

questions.q: An invoice-extraction pipeline defines one extraction tool, with tool_choice set to “auto”. On short or unusual documents, about 6% of the time, Claude replies in plain text (“This appears to be a receipt…”) instead of calling the tool, and the downstream parser crashes. What is the most direct fix?
opts: Add a system-prompt instruction saying the model must always call the extraction tool for every document.
Set tool_choice to “any”, so the model must call a tool instead of answering in text.
Catch text replies and resend the identical request until the model eventually calls the extraction tool.
Parse the plain-text replies with a regular expression to recover whatever fields the model mentioned.
questions.explain: With “auto” the model may answer in text. “any” guarantees a tool call, so every document produces structured output. A is a probabilistic instruction for something a setting can guarantee. C resends a request that behaves the same way. D builds a fragile parser around unstructured text.

questions.q: Incoming documents may be invoices, receipts or contracts, each with its own extraction tool and schema. The type isn't known in advance, and every document must produce structured output. Today tool_choice forces extract_invoice, and 40% of receipts and contracts come back with empty or wrong fields. How should tool_choice be set?
opts: “auto” with all three tools, so the model can pick a tool or explain in text when it's unsure of the type.
Forced to whichever tool matched the previous document, since batches tend to contain a single type.
“any” with all three tools, so the model must call one and chooses whichever tool fits the document.
Forced to extract_invoice as now, but with receipt and contract fields added to the invoice's schema.
questions.explain: “any” guarantees structured output and lets the model choose the schema that fits each document. A allows text replies, which breaks the every-document requirement. B and D keep forcing a single tool, so they either guess the type or push three schemas into one.

questions.q: In an extraction workflow, extract_metadata must run before anything else, because later tools depend on its output. After that, the model should choose freely between four enrichment tools or finish with a text answer. With tool_choice “auto” throughout, 12% of test runs skip extract_metadata. How should tool_choice be configured?
opts: Force extract_metadata on the first request, then use “auto” on the follow-up turns.
Use “any” on every turn, so the model always calls some tool and never skips a required step.
Keep “auto” throughout, and state in the system prompt that extract_metadata must be called first.
Force extract_metadata on every turn, so the metadata is always fresh before each enrichment call.
questions.explain: Forcing a specific tool on the first request guarantees that step runs, and “auto” afterwards gives back the freedom the later steps need. B guarantees some tool, not this one, and it also prevents the final text answer. C is prompt-based ordering, which already fails 12% of the time. D loops on the same tool forever.

questions.q: An extraction schema marks tax_id as a required string. An audit of 500 invoices finds plausible-looking tax IDs on 38 invoices that contain none, and every one of those outputs passed schema validation. What is the best schema change?
opts: Add a regex pattern to tax_id so that only correctly formatted tax IDs can pass schema validation.
Keep tax_id required, and say in the field description that the model must never invent a value.
Make tax_id optional or nullable, so that the model can report the value as absent from the document.
Add a confidence field next to tax_id, and drop any tax ID whose confidence the model rates below 0.7.
questions.explain: A required field forces the model to put something there. Making it nullable lets it say “not present”, which removes the pressure to invent a value. A: invented IDs are plausible, so a regex passes them. B leaves the pressure in place. D relies on self-reported confidence, which is poorly calibrated.

questions.q: A document_type enum lists invoice, receipt and contract. New document kinds, such as credit notes and delivery slips, keep being squeezed into “receipt”, and blurry scans are forced into a type too. Downstream, 7% of documents are routed to the wrong queue. What is the best schema design?
opts: Add every new document kind to the enum as it appears, and redeploy the schema each time one is found.
Replace the enum with a free-text string, so the model can describe each document in its own words.
Keep the enum, and add a system-prompt rule telling the model to choose the closest matching type.
Add “other” with a detail string for new kinds, and “unclear” for documents that can't be classified.
questions.explain: An “other” value with a detail string handles new kinds, and “unclear” gives ambiguous inputs an honest answer. Both keep the field structured and routable. A needs a redeploy for every new kind and still has no answer for blurry scans. B gives up the structure that routing depends on. C encourages the forced choice that causes the errors.

questions.q: In the research system, every agent is given all 18 tools. The synthesis agent runs its own web searches in about 40% of runs instead of synthesising what it was given, and those reports drift off-brief. What is the best change?
opts: Restrict each agent's tools to its role, so that the synthesis agent has no general web search tool.
Tell the synthesis agent in its system prompt that it must not search the web under any circumstances.
Add a PostToolUse hook that discards any web search results returned to the synthesis agent.
Reduce the synthesis agent's max_turns, so that it has no spare turns left for extra web searches.
questions.explain: Tools outside an agent's role invite misuse, so restricting tools by role removes the option altogether. B relies on the prompt being followed. C lets the search run and then throws the result away. D cuts the agent's legitimate work along with the misuse.

questions.q: In an extraction pipeline, a validation agent checks each invoice's totals. For 90% of invoices it only needs today's exchange rate for one currency pair, but every lookup goes through the coordinator to a finance-research agent, adding about 20 seconds per invoice. The other 10% need a real investigation of disputed historical rates. What is the best design?
opts: Give the validation agent all of the finance-research agent's tools, so it can handle every lookup itself.
Give the validation agent a narrowly scoped get_exchange_rate tool, and route investigations as before.
Pre-fetch exchange rates for every currency pair before each batch, so the validation agent never asks.
Batch all of a run's rate lookups into one coordinator request at the end of the validation pass.
questions.explain: A narrowly scoped cross-role tool covers the frequent simple case, while complex work keeps going through the coordinator. This is least privilege. A over-provisions the validation agent. C fetches rates nobody asked for. D creates a blocking dependency, because validation needs the rate before it can finish.

questions.q: A document-analysis subagent has a generic fetch_url tool. In about 1 run in 12, it fetches unrelated web pages, and occasionally tracking pixels, instead of the documents it was given. One run pulled 40 MB of unrelated content. What is the best fix?
opts: Add a line to the subagent's prompt telling it to fetch only the document URLs listed in its instructions.
Keep fetch_url, and add a size limit so that no single fetch can return more than 5 MB of content.
Log every fetch_url call, and review the log weekly to find and block domains it should not visit.
Replace fetch_url with a constrained load_document tool that only accepts and validates document URLs.
questions.explain: A generic tool is swapped for a constrained one that validates its input, which removes the misuse at the tool boundary. A relies on the prompt. B limits the damage but not the misuse. C finds the problem after the fact, one domain at a time.

questions.q: A single support agent has been given 18 tools as features were added: refunds, shipping, loyalty, marketing and analytics. Tool-selection errors have risen with each addition, from 3% at 5 tools to 14% today. Which design best restores reliability?
opts: Rewrite all 18 tool descriptions to be longer, so the model can distinguish between them more easily.
Upgrade to a larger model, which can reliably handle a bigger toolset without additional selection errors.
Split the work across focused agents, each with the 4–5 tools its job actually needs.
Add a keyword classifier that enables a different subset of the 18 tools for each incoming message.
questions.explain: Too many tools (18 instead of 4–5) degrades selection. Focused agents, each with a small role-specific tool set, fix the cause. A helps a little but doesn't change the number of choices. B relies on a bigger model to paper over a design problem. D adds a brittle keyword layer in front of the model.

questions.q: An extraction service that sets tool_choice {"type": "any"} starts returning HTTP 400 errors on every request after being moved to a newer model. The team's first idea is to retry each failed request with exponential backoff. What is the right adjustment?
opts: Keep the retries, since a 400 on a new model is usually temporary while capacity is provisioned.
Switch to a forced tool_choice naming the extraction tool, which every model accepts instead of “any”.
Move back to the previous model permanently, since the newer model can't produce structured output.
Use “auto” with strict tools, or structured outputs, on models that don't support forced tool use.
questions.explain: Some models reject forced tool use: both “any” and a named tool return a 400. The docs point to “auto” with strict tools, or to structured outputs. A retries a request that fails deterministically. B is also forced tool use, so it fails in the same way. C gives up a model that supports structured output another way.

faq.q: Why can't I get an explanation with a forced tool call?
faq.a: With any or tool the API prefills the assistant turn, so no text precedes the tool_use block. Use auto with an explicit instruction in the user message if you need both (docs).

faq.q: Does strict: true make the data correct?
faq.a: No. It guarantees the input matches the schema (types, required fields, valid tool name). Whether the total matches the line items is yours to validate — the exam's syntax-vs-semantics point.
The guide names auto, any and forced. none (no tools) comes from the docs; it is also the default when no tools are provided.

faq.q: Which models reject forced tool use?
faq.a: At the time of fetching (2026-09-27) the docs listed Claude Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1, plus manual extended thinking. Check the docs' table — it can change.

faq.q: How is load_document different from fetch_url?
faq.a: It's the guide's example of a constrained replacement for a generic tool: it only loads document URLs and rejects anything else, so an agent can't wander onto login pages or trackers.
